subject: arcticOutpost
pitch:
Category: Diorama.
Subject: arctic research outpost.
Style: Firewatch flat colour.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a single static TypeScript model for an arctic research outpost diorama — snow base, a cabin on stilts with glowing windows and a smoking chimney, a radio mast, a weather station, and a small sled, all built with plain geometry parts since no joints are needed.

Now I'm sketching out the Firewatch-inspired flat sunset palette with teal shadows and purple mountains, deciding scale (roughly a 4m cabin on a 12m snow disc), and writing simple box/cylinder helper functions to start assembling the base and cabin body.

Working out the cabin posts, gabled roof as an extruded triangular prism, and a snow-cap layer on top using tilted slab geometry with the correct slope angle.

Right side flips to +24.6°, with y centered at wallTop plus offset. Now I'm planning the facade details: a front door with frame, steps and railings, a porch platform, glowing windows with mullions and curtains on front and side walls, horizontal board stripes, cream corner trim, a chimney with low-poly smoke puffs, and a mast with guy wires.

I'm also laying out the surrounding scene: the mast with antenna crossbars and a red light near the cabin, a Stevenson screen weather station with an anemometer, a satellite dish on the roof or ground, orange and teal fuel drums with bands, a crate-laden sled, and a snowmobile.

Rounding out the diorama I'm adding pine trees near the back edge, purple faceted mountain cones with snow caps at the base rim beyond radius 6.5, a flag pole, a glowing lantern by the door, a firewood stack, snow drifts at the cabin base, and scattered rocks -- while settling on placing the cabin near the center of the 7.5-radius base.

Now I'm setting up small helper functions for building boxes, cylinders, cones, and spheres with position, color, and scale options, plus a glow wrapper to add light effects to parts, and defining a snow-themed color palette for the scene.

Still working out the cabin geometry...

Computing the snow offset along the roof normal so it sits just above the slab surface, nudging it slightly shorter in width than the roof so the eave edge peeks out, and planning small icicle cones hanging under the eave.

Now I'm laying out the front facade: a dark teal door with trim, a porch platform, and descending steps.

Then I'm adding railing posts at the porch corners, a small slanted awning over the door, and a glowing lantern sphere near the entrance, before moving on to place the front windows.

Each window gets a trim frame, glowing glass pane, dark mullions, a snow sill, and matching teal shutters, then I'm mirroring similar frames onto the side wall windows. Finally I'm adding thin horizontal wall board lines as subtle protruding slabs for texture.

Next I'm placing corner trim posts, a flattened snowdrift skirt around the foundation, and working out chimney placement on the right roof slab — calculating its height so it sits properly into the sloped surface, giving it a brick color and a dark cap.

I'm layering layered icosahedron spheres for smoke puffs rising from the chimney with increasing radius and soft pink-grey tones. Then I'm designing the radio mast: a tall lattice cylinder with a base, decreasing crossbars, a glowing red light on top, a horizontal dipole antenna, and guy wires anchoring down to the ground.

Nearby I'm adding a weather station setup -- a louvred Stevenson screen box on legs with a snow-capped roof, an anemometer pole with rotating cup arms and a wind vane, and a satellite dish on a pedestal using a partial sphere geometry for the dish shape.

Since a simple sphere cap only renders its outer convex face, I'm reworking the dish into a proper lathe-generated shell with both inner and outer profiles so the concave side faces upward and reads correctly from any angle.

Positioning the feed horn tip along the tilted axis, then placing three fuel drums with colored bands and lids off to one side, and finally laying out a sled with runners, a platform, and crates nearby.

For the snowmobile, since rotating a whole group is tricky with my helper functions, I'm keeping it axis-aligned facing forward and building it from separate boxes -- skis, tracks, body, hood, a thin tilted windshield, seat, and handlebars.

I'm checking placement coordinates so the snowmobile, stairs, sled, and dish don't overlap, then writing a pine tree helper that stacks a trunk cylinder with three snow-capped cones, and plotting out several tree positions around the scene's edges within the ground radius.

Now I'm positioning mountains as low-poly cones with snow-cap tops, making sure each one stays within the diorama boundary so none overhang the edge while still giving the background some depth.

Scaling the snow cap slightly larger than the cone to prevent z-fighting, then placing a flag pole with a red flag near the cabin front, adjusting the weather station and anemometer positions to avoid overlapping the cabin footprint.

Now I'm adding a firewood stack at the back-left wall using rotated cylinders arranged in rows, keeping the existing drums, and planning flattened spheres for snowdrifts and dark icosahedra for rocks scattered near the base.

I'm defining helper functions for spheres, cones, and cylinders that position objects based on a base coordinate and compute their center offsets, making sure everything sits above ground level starting from a base cylinder.

For the windmill, I'm figuring out rod connections between joints and planning the lathe-based dish shape, then working out the rotated arm boxes with cup spheres positioned around the pole using angular offsets.

With the geometry mapped out, I'm ready to write the final scene code, adding smoke as icosahedron spheres before wrapping things up.
